chevron.note: Two-step framework: if Congress has not directly spoken to the precise question, the court defers to the agency's reasonable interpretation of the statute it administers.

saucier.name: Saucier v. Katz, 533 U.S. 194 (2001)
saucier.note: Qualified immunity: the court first asks whether the facts show a constitutional violation; if so, it next asks whether the right was clearly established.

saucier.name: McClendon v. Story County Sheriff's Office
Kennedy ex rel. Gorton v. City of Ridgefield

teague.name: Teague v. Lane, 489 U.S. 288 (1989)
teague.note: New constitutional rules of criminal procedure generally do not apply on collateral review, except substantive rules and 'watershed rules of criminal procedure' implicating the fundamental fairness and accuracy of the proceeding.

teague.name: Fulcher v. Motley
teague.note: Cites Teague 35 times. The court: "holding that in habeas cases, a subsequently decided case does not present new law if it is "dictated by precedent existing at the time the defendant's conviction became final"".

roberts.name: Ohio v. Roberts, 448 U.S. 56 (1980)
roberts.note: An unavailable declarant's statement is admissible against the accused if it bears adequate indicia of reliability, inferred where it falls within a firmly rooted hearsay exception or shows particularized guarantees of trustworthiness.

roberts.name: United States v. Smith
roberts.note: Cites Ohio 95 times. The court: "noting that the "Framers' preference for face-to-face accusation" requires the proponent of recorded testimony to demonstrate unavailability of the witness, "including [in] cases where prior cross-exa".

roberts.name: Acosta v. Raemisch
roberts.note: Cites Ohio 36 times. The court: "Bea, J., concurring, in part and concurring in judgment".

roberts.name: Woodfox v. Cain
roberts.note: Cites Ohio 31 times. The court: ""At least since the decision of this Court in Mattox v. United States, 156 U.S. 237, 15 S.Ct. 337, 39 L.Ed. 409 (1895), prior-recorded testimony has been admissible in appropriate cases."".

roberts.name: Bockting v. Bayer
roberts.note: Cites Ohio 26 times. The court: "stating, the purpose of the Confrontation Clause is to "augment accuracy in the factfinding process"".

roberts.name: Fulcher v. Motley
roberts.note: Cites Ohio 21 times. The court: "holding that the Sixth Amendment requires that hearsay statements have "indicia of reliability" - i.e., either fall into a "firmly rooted hearsay exception" or have "particularized guarantees of trust".

casey.name: Planned Parenthood of Southeastern Pa. v. Casey, 505 U.S. 833 (1992)
casey.note: A state regulation of pre-viability abortion is invalid if its purpose or effect is to place a substantial obstacle in the path of a woman seeking an abortion (the undue burden standard).

williamson.name: Williamson County Regional Planning Comm'n v. Hamilton Bank, 473 U.S. 172 (1985)
williamson.note: A takings claim is not ripe until the government entity has reached a final decision and the owner has sought compensation through the procedures the State provides.

lemon.name: Lemon v. Kurtzman, 403 U.S. 602 (1971)
lemon.note: Government action must have a secular legislative purpose, a principal or primary effect that neither advances nor inhibits religion, and must not foster an excessive government entanglement with religion.

lemon.name: Skoros v. City of New York
lemon.note: Cites Lemon 32 times. The court: "requiring challenged action to (1) have a valid secular purpose, (2) have a primary effect that neither advances nor inhibits religion, and (3) avoid excessive state entanglement with religion".

abood.name: Abood v. Detroit Board of Education, 431 U.S. 209 (1977)
abood.note: Public employees who are not union members may be required to pay a service fee covering the union's collective-bargaining, contract-administration and grievance costs, but not its political or ideological activities.
